title: WPSS/1149/2006 of SMT. SUJATA Vs STATE and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE H IGH COU RT O F UTTARANCHAL
AT NA IN ITAL
Writ Petition No. 1149 (SS) of 2006
Smt. Sujata,
W/o Sri Vinay Singh,
R/o 4, Doon Enclave,
Simla Road,
Dehradun ÖÖ...Petitioner.
Versus
1. State of Uttarakhand through Secretary Intermediate
Education, Dehradun.
2. Uttaranchal Public Service Commission, Hardwar
through its Secretary.
ÖÖÖ.Respondents
Honíble M.M. Ghildiyal, J
Heard Sri Lok Pal Singh, learned counsel for the
petitioner, Sri N.P. Shah, learned standing counsel for State of
Uttarakhand on behalf of respondent no. 1 and Sri B.D.
Kandpal, learned counsel for respondent no. 2.
By means of this writ petition, the petitioners have
prayed for the following reliefs:
1. Issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
Mandamus commanding the respondents to give an
appointment o the post of Lecturer Geography in
pursuance of the result dated 23.07.2005 contained
Annexure no.5 to the writ petition.
2. issue any other relief, which this Honíble court may deem
fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.
3. cost of the petition be awarded in favour of the petitioner.

2
In pursuance to the advertisement dated 30.10.2003
applications were invited for the posts of Lecturer in
Intermediate Colleges by Public Service Commission.
Petitioner being fully qualified and eligible applied for
the said post. Petitioner has been selected being OBC candidate,
after qualifying written test and interview for the post of
Lecturer (Geography).
Petitioner was permanent resident of Saharanpur, Uttar
Pradesh and belongs to Gujar caste, which comes under OBC
category in the State of U.P. Petitioner got married with one Sri
Vinay Singh, who is permanent resident of Village ñ Dhadheki,
Tehsil ñ Laksar, District Hardwar and also belongs to Gujar
caste, which also comes under OBC Category in State of
Uttarakhand.
By giving benefit under U.P. Public Services (Reservation
for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and other Backward
Classes), Act, 1994 petitioner was selected provisionally by
respondent no.2 and respondent no.2 recommended the name
of the petitioner including others for appointment as Lecturer
in the Intermediate College of State of Uttarakhand. Others
persons, who had been selected with the petitioners have been
given appointment, however, the Government has still not
issued appointment letter to the petitioner.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that it
appears that Government has not issued appointment letter to
the petitioner in view of the fact that petitioner has obtained
two caste certificates one from Saharanpur Authorities and
another from Tehsildar ñ Laksar, District ñ Hardwar.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that
petitioner belongs to Gujar Caste which comes in OBC category

3
in the both the States i.e. in the State of Uttarakhand and State
of U.P. and petitioner has married with a person who belong to
Gujar Caste in District ñ Hardwar, even then petitioner is not
being issued appointment letter.
Petitioner has already made undated representation
before secretary Education, Dehradun, which is annexed as
Annexure no. 6 to the writ petition.
Petitioner is directed to make fresh representation before
respondent no. 1 i.e. Secretary Education, State of Uttarakhand
raising all her grievances within a period of two weeks from
today and the Secretary Education, State of Uttarakhand is
directed to take decision within a period of three weeks from
the date of production of certified copy of this order along with
representation. If respondent no. 1 finds that petitioner is
entitled for appointment, he will issue necessary appointment
letter forthwith.
With this direction, writ petition as well as interim relief
application no. 10764 of 2006 is finally disposed of. No order as
to costs.
(M.M. Ghildiyal, J)
March 15, 2007
Sksharma
